abstract: P-glycoprotein (Pgp/ABCB1) is a critical efflux transporter that significantly impacts drug bioavailability and multidrug resistance. Accurate prediction of Pgp substrate status is essential for early-stage drug discovery. In this study, we evaluate a pretrained Graph Iso-morphism Network (GIN) with attribute masking on the Pgp_Broccatelli benchmark from the Therapeutics Data Commons (TDC). Our approach fine-tunes a GIN encoder pretrained on approximately 2 million molecules using a self-supervised attribute masking strategy, followed by a multilayer perceptron (MLP) classification head. On the TDC benchmark, our model achieves an AUROC of 0.937 {+/-} 0.004 across five independent runs, ranking second on the leaderboard, as of May 2026. We further compare this approach against an XGBoost baseline using Morgan fingerprints (AUROC 0.912 {+/-} 0.007), demonstrating the advantage of graph-based molecular representations with transfer learning for small-dataset ADMET prediction tasks.
